title: Empty circular waveguide, radius 10 mm, 30 mm long, on a quarter (rotational symmetry C4): rotating TE11+, TM01 and TE21+ transmission
source: Circular waveguide modes, S21 = exp(−jβL) with β = √(k0² − (x/a)²), x = x'₁₁ = 1.841183781340659 (TE11), x₀₁ = 2.404825557695773 (TM01), x'₂₁ = 3.054236928227140 (TE21) (M. Abramowitz, I. A. Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, 1964, Table 9.5; D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §3.4); a rotating mode e^{∓jnφ} is the sum of the two standing polarizations with a quarter-period between them and propagates alike

quantities.quantity: phase of S21 at 10.5 GHz, TE11+ (degrees)
quantities.reason: 3 mm tetrahedra of one quarter, second order, the wall curved: +0.04° over 30 mm near cut-off, as the whole guide (`circular-guide`, +0.03°)
lossless: power is conserved; |S21| moves only by the small reflection
the rotating Bessel modes at the ports against the sector's curved cross-section: 6e-5

quantities.quantity: phase of S21 at 13.5 GHz, TE11+ (degrees)
quantities.reason: as at 10.5 GHz, farther from cut-off: +0.06°

quantities.quantity: phase of S21 at 14 GHz, TM01 (degrees)
quantities.reason: harmonic 0 on the same mesh (only the cut faces' phase moves): +0.04°

quantities.quantity: phase of S21 at 17 GHz, TE21+ (degrees)
quantities.reason: harmonic 2: two azimuthal periods over the turn, half of one across the quarter, the coarsest-resolved mode here: +0.26° (converging as the mesh is refined)
